description.narrative: Goal The main objective of the intervention is to improve conditions in Bolivian watersheds by sustainably and resiliently managing water resources to improve human health and well-being, agricultural productivity, energy production and ecosystem function to improve livelihoods for all watershed residents. This will be done through the creation of an enabling environment to operationalize the National Watershed Plan in a way that allows sustainable sanitation to be fully considered as an essential component of integrated water resource management. The intervention has three specific outcomes with associated indicators: 1. The production of Watershed Master Plans the actually prioritize implementable water management strategies based on an informed participatory process. Indicator: Three (3) Watershed Master Plans (PDCs) completed with specific project opportunities identified and prioritized 2. Water management strategies prioritized in Watershed Master Plans will include sustainable sanitation solution, along with other water management actions. Indicator: At least one (1) sustainable sanitation opportunity included in the first set of priority projects selected for potential funding in each PDC developed. 3. Conditions conducive to expanding sustainable sanitation solutions in Bolivian watersheds will be created. Indicator: Capacity successfully developed, based on demonstrable success in the three pilot watershed systems to: a. Connect WEAP and REVAMP (tools developed by SEI in decision making and resource allocation) deployed at the watershed level to the BHSB b. Run a participatory process in support of the PDC development effort using the Robust Desicion Support (RDS) approach. c. Implement, maintain, and economically operate waste collection and reuse technologies.

Stockholm Environment Institute (SEI) har inkommit med ett programförslag för programmet "WASH thinking connected to Hydrology" och ansökt om programstöd, 45 MSEK under åren 2018-2021. WATCH kommer under de närmaste 3,5 åren att förbättra villkoren för Bolivinaska avrinningsområden genom hållbar vattenresurshantering för att förbättra hälsa ich välmående, jordbruksproduktion, energiproduktion och ekosystemfunktioner för at förbättra levnadsstandarden för alla invånare runt de tre strategiskt utvalda avrinningsområdena. Programvisionen är att ge Bolivianska institutioner tillräckligt med information och kapacitet för att knyta samman två för tillfället och historiskt separerade områden (WASH och vattenresurshantering) och på så sätt få kunna fatta mer inkluderande, miljömässigt och politiskt hållbara beslut inom vattenresurshantering.
Programmet är strukturerat kring de sju pelarna i Bolivias nationella plan för avrinningsområden (PNC). 1.Förvaltning av strategiska avrinningsområden genom utvecklandet av lokala styrplaner (PDCs)Management of strategic watersheds through the development of PDCs. 2.Investeringar i hållbar vattenresursförvaltning 3.Förvaltning av hydrologiska risker och klimatförändringar 4.Vattenkvalitets förvaltning. 5.Interkulturellt lärande genom utbyte mellan avrinningsområden 6.Hydro-ekologisk information och kommunikation 7.Kapacitetsbyggande och institutionell utveckling/förstärkning relaterad till förvaltning av hydro-ekologi.
Programmet har tre tematiska och en övergripande komponent som tillsammans ämnar nå det övergripande programmålet "Att förbättra förhållanden i Bolivianska avrinningsområden genom att hållbart och resilient sköta vattenresurser för att förbättra hälsa och välmående, produktivitet i jordbruket, energiproduktion och ekosystemfunktioner för att förbättra liven för alla invånare kring avrinningsområden".
Komponent 1: Förhållanden i avrinningsområden Denna komponent ämnar undersöka och skapa verktyg för att analysera förhållanden i avrinningsområden, framförallt fokuserat på vatten balans och vattenkvalitet.
Komponent2: Alternativ för hantering av vattenresurser. Denna komponent fokuserar på processer och system kring beslutsfattande. Programmet ämnar utveckla processer och system för att brygga gapet mellan beslutsfattande inom Vatten och sanitet och vattenresurshantering och bevattning och föra samman utvecklingsprocesserna av PDCs och vattenförsörjningsplanerna för städer. Denna komponent inkluderar ett aktivt arbeta och deltagande av olika berörda grupper och SEI kommer aktivt att arbeta med jämställdhets och fattigdomsanalys.
Komponent 3: Alternativ för hållbara sanitetslösningar Komponenten fokuserar på implementering och uppskalning av hållbara sanitetsmodeller, vattenkvalitet och återanvändning av vatten och näringsämnen. Sverige har länge och fortsätter att arbeta med bland annat organisationen Agua Tuya och UNICEF inom detta område och SEIs arbete ämnar komplementera detta arbete bland annat genom tekniskt stöd.
Den övergripande komponenten "Master component" ämnar koppla ihop de tre tematiska komponenterna och skapa en strukturerad förhandlingsprocess inom vattenresurshantering som inkluderar deltagande och röster från berörda grupper, marginaliserade samhällen och grupper och som tar hänsyn till miljöpåverkan.

Stockholm Environment Institute has submitted a proposal to the Embassy for support to the programme Wash thinking connected to Hydrology (WATCH) WATCH will over the course of the next 3, 5 years to improve conditions in Bolivian watersheds by sustainably and resiliently managing water resources and sanitation systems to improve human health and wellbeing, agricultural productivity, energy production and ecosystem function to improve livelihoods for all watershed residents. For the programme period, from June 2018 to 2021, the amount requested from Sweden is 45 million SEK. The programme is structured around the seven main pillars of the national watershed plan. The primary program component under the programme WATCH will be policy engagement, designed to connect currently separate WASH and watershed planning with the decision-making processes and support the development and articulation of national, departmental and municipal guidelines and norms that encourage connections between these two policy areas. In order to insure the long-term strength of these connections, Bolivia WATCH will also include activities designed to strengthen the capacity of key actors within the WASH and watershed arenas. The vision for the proposed program is that it will give the relevant Bolivian institutions the information and capacity required to fully connect what have historically be separated decision-making related to WASH and watershed once the period of program implementation ends.

sector.narrative: Water supply and sanitation - large systems

description.narrative:
The main result has been the development of the 3 Master Watershed Plans (Planes Directores de Cuenca PDC) for Tupiza, Pampa Huari and Río La Paz.
However, behind the construction of these plans, a lot of work has been required. This has led to specific results that is important to specify.
1. Strengthening Water Governance among Local Partners • Bolivia WATCH has promoted the formal constitution and institutionalization of three Inter-institutional Basin Management Platforms. These Platforms are currently effective mechanisms for managing governance in basins. • Bolivia WATCH has promoted inter-governmental dialogue in each basin, between Municipal Governments (GAM by Spanish mean) and Departmental Government (GAD by Spanish mean); but it has also promoted dialogue with the Vice Ministry of Water Resources and Irrigation (VRHR) as head of sector. In all three basins these dialogues were less frequent before Bolivia WATCH. • In the specific case of the Department of Potosí, having worked the Tupiza and Pampa Huari basins; the discussion of a departmental bill that prioritizes the execution of the PDCs has been promoted.
2. Technical capacity building and social participation/inclusion • 2032 people have been trained, with topics ranging from technical to management. The Training Program for "Water Quality Monitors" and the "Management of drones for water surveillance" priority was given to the participation of women from the communities of the basins. In the case of the course of water quality monitors, the protocols have been adopted as a water surveillance mechanism by the Autonomous Municipal Government of Tupiza. • Bolivia WATCH has also facilitated specific technical training skills at the university level, through 2 diplomas with public universities in Bolivia (with the participation of 54 professionals). With the Universidad Mayor de San Andrés (UMSA) the Diploma in "Wastewater Processing for Reuse in Agricultural Irrigation" and with the Gabriel René Moreno Autonomous University (UAGRM) the Diploma in WEAP was organized • More than 60 Municipal/departmental/WASH utilities technicians of the area of intervention have been trained in topics of: Hydroclimatic risk assessment, hydrological modelling, geospatial information management, public investment planning management and financing management. This set of topics has had an impact on the formulation of the (Territorial Plans for Integral Development (PTDI), given that the technicians have included some actions of the PDCs of their respective basins in the Municipal planning (PTDI and POA )
3. Development of tailor-made scientific tools • The formulation of the PDCs and the enabling conditions for their implementation have been the setting to produce a scientific, analytical, and visual Toolbox, which are a contribution to the knowledge and instrumentation of the sector. Around WEAP (Water Evaluation And Planning System), a platform developed by SEI more than 20 years ago, new tools have been coupled to give more robustness to planning, simulation of actions and evaluation of responses in scenarios that consider climate change. The Toolbox integrated by WEAP , REVAMP , WashFlows , WaTT , EWI , k-NN and MTDP make up an ecosystem capable of analysing the characteristics of the basin from water sources, the demands for different uses, the topography of the basin, the integration of water flows and sanitation in the basin, the empowerment of marginalized populations in water management , the impact of climate change that will nuance the proposals for solutions and investments. The Watershed Viceministry is considering this toolbox to be the official instrument to monitor the goals and indicators of the new National Watershed Plan (Plan Plurinacional de Recursos Hídricos) PPRH and other sectoral indicators that contribute to the Socio -Economic Plan. In addition, these tools will be part of the Observatory proposed by the PPRH and contents to be amplified through the Pedagogical Basins of the PPRH. • A digital visualization platform of the basins has been developed for the PDCs and Chiquitanía (based on the ThingLink software). Its objectives is to locate the problems and the actions proposed for the improvement in the PDCs with 360 and 3D photographs. This platform will be adopted by the VRHR to represent the 19 current PDCs and will be called "Digital Basin" • 3 Geographic Atlas and Geodata bases have been generated for each of the Basins, being the basis of information for public investment and planning projects. • For the sub-basins of the Chiquitanía (WATCH Chiquitanía) a visualization platform was developed based on Tableau software, this tool allows the visualization of the impact of fires on environmental conditions and the quality and availability of water resources.
4. Financial Mechanism for the implementation of PDC • Bolivia WATCH has carried out a complete study to identify sources of financing (of different nature: national public, private, cooperation) and the respective procedures to be carried out for the implementation of the PDCs. In addition, a tutorial guide for financing management has been developed. • The Municipal Government of Yocalla (Pampa Huari Basin), has leveraged funds from the Indigenous Fund for two project proposals in their plan. One for irrigation and another for sanitation
5. Gender and poverty • Bolivia WATCH Programme worked in GESEP, a tool to analyse water-related vulnerabilities through the lens of the multi-dimensional poverty analysis (MDPA) at the community level. The analysis involved developing and adapting methodologies to examine the connections between water access and people's livelihoods, including gender equality and poverty, based on the unique context and data at hand. All the results have been included in the PDCs.
6.Sustainable Sanitation • Connecting WASH to watershed planning: A key innovation scope of the programme was to include sustainable water supply and sanitation actions within the set of water management innovations evaluated within a PDC, although such innovations are within the institutional mandate of a separate vice-ministry from the vice-ministry responsible for PDCs. This gave further credibility to long-standing efforts to convey to the VAPSB the potential usefulness of sustainable sanitation options. For this, the WASHFlows and REVAMP tools were developed and integrated into the WEAP tool. • Complementarity was achieved for the first time (in the Pampa Huari Basin Municipality of Potosí) of a Basin Master Plan with a Master Plan for Drinking Water and Basic Sanitation. The impact of this connection is the institutionalization of efforts through the coordination of municipal and departmental basin technicians with technicians from the Public Water and Sanitation Company • Specific sanitation solutions (such as improvement in sewage systems, decentralized wastewater treatment plant, domestic wetlands) have been identified and developed in the three developed PDC • In collaboration with the UAGRM, 3 investigations have been developed in the city of Montero to understand the acceptance of decentralized sustainable sanitation systems. This understanding has guided the formulation of PDCs.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
